title: fleet upgrade --apply rewrites an estate's vendored runtime under a live dispatch -- it should refuse that estate by name
body:
## What happens

`bin/devbin fleet upgrade --apply` rewrites `bin/devbin` and `bin/.devbin/lib/` in every estate it sweeps and checks nothing about what is running there. Bash reads a script as it executes it, so a dispatch in flight while its handler is replaced can run text that is half the old file and half the new one (the hazard lamplight-vc named on 2026-09-22). For the 0.1.6 and 0.1.7 sweeps the check was made by hand before `--apply` (`ps -eo pid=,args=` for `bin/devbin` and `dvb`, cwd per process). Nothing in the verb makes it.

## What should happen

`--apply` refuses, by name, any estate with a live `bin/devbin` or `dvb` dispatch, naming the process id and command, and sweeps the rest. The dry run reports the same condition as a row in "Not swept -- named rather than dropped", so the preview and the apply agree. Matching is by process cwd inside the estate, read from the process table by `args`, never `comm` (bats and devbin are bash scripts; `comm` reads `bash`).

## Ruling

hv, 2026-09-22 ~21:00Z: yes, file and build it, and ship it in the next patch. It is an issue, not a thread. Filed by vc, for building on 2026-09-23.


## Resolution

Closed 2026-09-23 on hv's ruling, not built. hv's words: "Ok, close it. It seems like a very low risk." and "I think we can close it on my fiat as not needed." hv's reason: the exposure came from five or six live projects running while devbin was being upgraded under them, which is not the normal state, and it ends once devbin and Intent settle.

THE MECHANISM UNDER "What happens" IS REFUTED, and this section is the correction to it. `copy_vendored` in `lib/install` replaces an existing vendored file through a temporary beside it and `mv -f`, a rename, so the file gets a new inode while a running bash keeps reading the old one through its open descriptor. Measured by vc on 2026-09-23 in scratch, one run per arm, on macOS with bash 5. CONTROL: a running script rewritten in place, same inode, read the new bytes at its old offset and died with `unexpected EOF`, rc=2, so the probe can show a torn read. SUBJECT: the same script replaced by `copy_vendored`, sourced from the tree, got a new inode and finished its old text, rc=0. Not driven on Linux, where rename carries the same POSIX semantics.

WHAT REMAINS, deliberately not built for, is version skew. A run that reads a file after the sweep has replaced it gets the new bytes: a late `source` read the new file in the same probe. devbin's own indented sources in `lib/help`, `lib/resolve` and `lib/runlog` are load-time include guards, so a dispatch reads its libraries as it starts, and a live run spans two versions only if it launches a child dispatch after the sweep reaches its estate -- a config `run:` row calling `bin/devbin`, for instance. A hand check before a sweep still covers that, and it has to match `bin/.devbin/` as well as `bin/devbin` and `dvb`: the launcher `exec`s its handler (`exec_handler` in `lib/resolve`), so a dispatch in flight carries its handler's path in `args`, not the launcher's. That last point is read from the source, not driven.
